level_1() {
  TITLE="Hello, ed"
  BRIEF="The buffer is empty. Type the line 'Hello, world!' into it.
Use ${B}a${N} to start appending text, type your line, then a lone ${B}.${N}
on its own line to stop. Then ${B}w${N} to write and ${B}q${N} to quit."
  START=''
  TARGET='Hello, world!'
  HINT="a  ⏎  Hello, world!  ⏎  .  ⏎  w  ⏎  q"
  SOLUTION=$'a\nHello, world!\n.\nw\nq'
}

level_2() {
  TITLE="Exterminate"
  BRIEF="Something has infiltrated the fruit list. Delete it.
Commands take ${B}addresses${N}: '3d' deletes line 3."
  START=$'apples\nbananas\nDELETE ME\ncherries'
  TARGET=$'apples\nbananas\ncherries'
  HINT="The intruder is on line 3. Address + command: 3d"
  SOLUTION=$'3d\nw\nq'
}

level_3() {
  TITLE="Tail End"
  BRIEF="You forgot the butter. Append it to the end of the list.
${B}\$${N} is the address of the last line."
  START=$'eggs\nmilk\nbread'
  TARGET=$'eggs\nmilk\nbread\nbutter'
  HINT="\$a appends after the last line. (After loading a file the current
line is already the last one, so a plain 'a' works too.)"
  SOLUTION=$'a\nbutter\n.\nw\nq'
}

level_4() {
  TITLE="First Things First"
  BRIEF="This TODO list has no heading. Insert '# TODO' as the very first line.
${B}i${N} inserts text ${I}before${N} the addressed line."
  START=$'- learn ed\n- learn more ed\n- become ed'
  TARGET=$'# TODO\n- learn ed\n- learn more ed\n- become ed'
  HINT="1i inserts before line 1. (0a — append after line zero — also works.)"
  SOLUTION=$'1i\n# TODO\n.\nw\nq'
}

level_5() {
  TITLE="Placeholder"
  BRIEF="Replace the three lorem-ipsum lines with the single line
'content goes here'. ${B}c${N} changes (replaces) a range of lines.
Ranges look like ${B}2,4${N}."
  START=$'BEGIN\nlorem ipsum\ndolor sit amet\nconsectetur\nEND'
  TARGET=$'BEGIN\ncontent goes here\nEND'
  HINT="2,4c  then type the replacement, then a lone '.'"
  SOLUTION=$'2,4c\ncontent goes here\n.\nw\nq'
}

level_6() {
  TITLE="Quick Fox"
  BRIEF="The fox has upgraded. Change 'jumps' to 'leaps gracefully'.
${B}s/old/new/${N} substitutes on the addressed line."
  START=$'The quick brown fox\njumps over\nthe lazy dog'
  TARGET=$'The quick brown fox\nleaps gracefully over\nthe lazy dog'
  HINT="2s/jumps/leaps gracefully/"
  SOLUTION=$'2s/jumps/leaps gracefully/\nw\nq'
}

level_7() {
  TITLE="Colour Me American"
  BRIEF="Americanize every 'colour' (any case, every occurrence) to 'color'.
Leave 'favourite' alone — we're not monsters.
The address ${B},${N} means every line (1,\$). The ${B}g${N} suffix on s means
every match on the line, not just the first."
  START=$'The colour of the sky.\nMy favourite colour is blue, not that colour.\nColourless green ideas sleep furiously.'
  TARGET=$'The color of the sky.\nMy favourite color is blue, not that color.\nColorless green ideas sleep furiously.'
  HINT="Match the part that's the same in 'colour' and 'Colour': ,s/olour/olor/g"
  SOLUTION=$',s/olour/olor/g\nw\nq'
}

level_8() {
  TITLE="No Comment"
  BRIEF="Strip every comment line (lines starting with #) from this config.
${B}g/re/cmd${N} runs cmd on every line matching the regex re."
  START=$'# config file\nname=ed\n# the standard editor\nversion=1.0\n# end of file\nmode=fast'
  TARGET=$'name=ed\nversion=1.0\nmode=fast'
  HINT="^ anchors a regex to the start of the line:  g/^#/d"
  SOLUTION=$'g/^#/d\nw\nq'
}

level_9() {
  TITLE="Signal, Not Noise"
  BRIEF="Your boss only wants the ERROR lines from this log. Delete everything else.
${B}v/re/cmd${N} is the inverse of g: it runs cmd on lines that ${I}don't${N} match."
  START=$'INFO  boot ok\nERROR disk on fire\nDEBUG x=3\nINFO  user logged in\nERROR printer achieved sentience\nWARN  coffee low\nERROR coffee empty'
  TARGET=$'ERROR disk on fire\nERROR printer achieved sentience\nERROR coffee empty'
  HINT="v/ERROR/d"
  SOLUTION=$'v/ERROR/d\nw\nq'
}

level_10() {
  TITLE="Breakfast Is Served"
  BRIEF="This recipe says to eat the pancakes before making them. Fix the order.
${B}m${N} moves lines: '1m3' moves line 1 to after line 3."
  START=$'Eat the pancakes.\nMix flour, eggs, and milk.\nPour batter into a hot pan.\nFlip when bubbles appear.'
  TARGET=$'Mix flour, eggs, and milk.\nPour batter into a hot pan.\nFlip when bubbles appear.\nEat the pancakes.'
  HINT="Move line 1 to after the last line: 1m\$"
  SOLUTION=$'1m$\nw\nq'
}

level_11() {
  TITLE="Sing It Again"
  BRIEF="Songs repeat the chorus. Copy the chorus to the end of the song.
${B}t${N} (transfer) copies lines: '2t\$' copies line 2 after the last line."
  START=$'Verse one: I opened a file\nCHORUS: oh ed, oh ed, you print only ?\nVerse two: I typed :wq out of habit'
  TARGET=$'Verse one: I opened a file\nCHORUS: oh ed, oh ed, you print only ?\nVerse two: I typed :wq out of habit\nCHORUS: oh ed, oh ed, you print only ?'
  HINT="2t\$"
  SOLUTION=$'2t$\nw\nq'
}

level_12() {
  TITLE="Supercalifragilistic"
  BRIEF="A word got shattered across four lines. Glue it back together.
${B}j${N} joins a range of lines into one (with no separator)."
  START=$'super\ncali\nfragilistic\nexpialidocious'
  TARGET='supercalifragilisticexpialidocious'
  HINT="1,4j   — or just ,j"
  SOLUTION=$',j\nw\nq'
}

level_13() {
  TITLE="Identity Crisis"
  BRIEF="Convert 'Last, First' into 'First Last' for every pioneer — in one command.
Capture groups are ${B}\\(...\\)${N} and are referenced as ${B}\\1${N}, ${B}\\2${N}."
  START=$'Turing, Alan\nHopper, Grace\nLovelace, Ada\nRitchie, Dennis\nThompson, Ken'
  TARGET=$'Alan Turing\nGrace Hopper\nAda Lovelace\nDennis Ritchie\nKen Thompson'
  HINT=",s/\\(.*\\), \\(.*\\)/\\2 \\1/"
  SOLUTION=$',s/\\(.*\\), \\(.*\\)/\\2 \\1/\nw\nq'
}

level_14() {
  TITLE="Significant Whitespace"
  BRIEF="This Python function body isn't indented. Indent lines 2 through the end
by exactly four spaces. (^ matches the empty spot at the start of a line.)"
  START=$'def greet(name):\nmessage = "Hello, " + name\nprint(message)\nreturn message'
  TARGET=$'def greet(name):\n    message = "Hello, " + name\n    print(message)\n    return message'
  HINT="2,\$s/^/    /"
  SOLUTION=$'2,$s/^/    /\nw\nq'
}

level_15() {
  TITLE="Invisible Enemies"
  BRIEF="Trailing whitespace (shown highlighted in ${HL} red ${N}) is lurking at the
ends of lines. Some are spaces, some are tabs. Destroy it all."
  START=$'int main(void) {   \n\tint x = 42;\t\n\treturn x;  \t \n}'
  TARGET=$'int main(void) {\n\tint x = 42;\n\treturn x;\n}'
  HINT="[[:blank:]] matches a space or tab; * means zero or more; \$ anchors
to end of line:   ,s/[[:blank:]]*\$//"
  SOLUTION=$',s/[[:blank:]]*$//\nw\nq'
}

level_16() {
  TITLE="Backwards Day"
  BRIEF="Reverse the order of every line in the file.
There's a famous one-liner for this. Think about g and m together."
  START=$'one\ntwo\nthree\nfour\nfive\nliftoff'
  TARGET=$'liftoff\nfive\nfour\nthree\ntwo\none'
  HINT="If you move each line, top to bottom, to the very top of the file
(after line 0), what happens?   g/^/m0"
  SOLUTION=$'g/^/m0\nw\nq'
}

level_17() {
  TITLE="Sign Here"
  BRIEF="Your letter needs a signature. The file ${B}signature.txt${N} is sitting in the
same directory. Read its contents into the end of the buffer.
${B}r file${N} reads a file in after the addressed line."
  START=$'Dear Ken,\n\nThanks for ed. It is very standard.\n'
  TARGET=$'Dear Ken,\n\nThanks for ed. It is very standard.\n\n-- \nA. User\nSent from my teletype'
  HINT="\$r signature.txt"
  SOLUTION=$'$r signature.txt\nw\nq'
  EXTRA_NAME="signature.txt"
  EXTRA_CONTENT=$'-- \nA. User\nSent from my teletype'
}

level_18() {
  TITLE="Range Rover"
  BRIEF="The Body section ended up after the Conclusion. Move the whole Body
section (heading and contents) so it comes right after the Intro section.
Ranges work with m too. Regex addresses like ${B}/Body/${N} work as well."
  START=$'## Intro\nhello\n## Conclusion\nbye\n## Body\nstuff\nmore stuff'
  TARGET=$'## Intro\nhello\n## Body\nstuff\nmore stuff\n## Conclusion\nbye'
  HINT="Lines 5 through 7 should go after line 2:  5,7m2  (or /Body/,\$m2)"
  SOLUTION=$'5,$m2\nw\nq'
}

level_19() {
  TITLE="Double Spaced"
  BRIEF="Your professor wants double spacing. Put an empty line between every pair
of lines — but ${I}not${N} after the last line.
Secret technique: a backslash-newline in the replacement of s splits a line."
  START=$'It was a dark and stormy night.\nThe editor printed a single ?\nAnd nothing more.'
  TARGET=$'It was a dark and stormy night.\n\nThe editor printed a single ?\n\nAnd nothing more.'
  HINT="Address every line except the last: 1,\$-1   then
  1,\$-1s/\$/\\     ⏎   /"
  SOLUTION=$'1,$-1s/$/\\\n/\nw\nq'
}

level_20() {
  TITLE="FINAL BOSS: The Shopping List"
  BRIEF="Everything is wrong. Make it right:
  • the heading must read '# Shopping List'
  • the comment line must go
  • every 'eggz' must become 'eggs'
  • '- butter' must be appended at the end
Combine everything you've learned. Par is tight."
  START=$'# shopping lsit\n- milk\n- eggz\n# comment: delete me\n- bread\n- eggz'
  TARGET=$'# Shopping List\n- milk\n- eggs\n- bread\n- eggs\n- butter'
  HINT="1s/s.*/Shopping List/   g/comment/d   ,s/eggz/eggs/   \$a ... ."
  SOLUTION=$'1s/s.*/Shopping List/\ng/comment/d\n,s/eggz/eggs/\n$a\n- butter\n.\nw\nq'
}

NUM_LEVELS=$(declare -F | grep -c ' level_[0-9]*$')

load_level() {
  TITLE='' BRIEF='' START='' TARGET='' HINT='' SOLUTION='' EXTRA_NAME='' EXTRA_CONTENT=''
  "level_$1"
  PAR=$(printf '%s\n' "$SOLUTION" | wc -l)
}

# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  SAVE DATA   (one "level best_count" pair per line)
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

get_best() {
  [[ -f "$SAVE_FILE" ]] || return 0
  awk -v l="$1" '$1 == l { print $2 }' "$SAVE_FILE"
}

set_best() {
  mkdir -p "$SAVE_DIR"
  local tmp="$SAVE_FILE.tmp"
  { [[ -f "$SAVE_FILE" ]] && awk -v l="$1" '$1 != l' "$SAVE_FILE"; echo "$1 $2"; } > "$tmp"
  mv "$tmp" "$SAVE_FILE"
}

stars_for() { # count par
  local c=$1 p=$2
  if   (( c <= p ));     then echo 3
  elif (( c <= p + 2 )); then echo 2
  else                        echo 1
  fi
}

star_string() {
  local n=$1 s='' i
  for ((i = 1; i <= 3; i++)); do
    if (( i <= n )); then s+="${YEL}★${N}"; else s+="${D}☆${N}"; fi
  done
  printf '%s' "$s"
}

level_stars() { # level -> 0..3
  local best; best=$(get_best "$1")
  [[ -z "$best" ]] && { echo 0; return; }
  load_level "$1"
  stars_for "$best" "$PAR"
}

total_stars() {
  local t=0 i
  for ((i = 1; i <= NUM_LEVELS; i++)); do (( t += $(level_stars "$i") )); done
  echo "$t"
}

rank_for() {
  local s=$1 max=$((NUM_LEVELS * 3))
  if   (( s == 0 ));         then echo "?"
  elif (( s < 10 ));         then echo "Teletype Tourist"
  elif (( s < 25 ));         then echo "Line Addresser"
  elif (( s < 40 ));         then echo "Regex Wrangler"
  elif (( s < 55 ));         then echo "Bell Labs Intern"
  elif (( s < max ));        then echo "Ken Thompson's Understudy"
  else                            echo "THE STANDARD TEXT EDITOR"
  fi
}

# Print a file's contents with line numbers; trailing whitespace highlighted,
# tabs shown as → so invisible stuff is visible.
show_text() { # label color text
  local label=$1 color=$2 text=$3
  printf '  %s%s┌─ %s%s\n' "$color" "$B" "$label" "$N"
  if [[ -z "$text" ]]; then
    printf '  %s│%s %s(empty file)%s\n' "$color" "$N" "$D" "$N"
  else
    printf '%s\n' "$text" | awk -v c="$color" -v n="$N" -v hl="$HL" -v d="$D" '
      {
        line = $0
        match(line, /[ \t]+$/)
        body = (RSTART ? substr(line, 1, RSTART - 1) : line)
        tail = (RSTART ? substr(line, RSTART) : "")
        gsub(/\t/, d "→" n "   ", body)
        gsub(/\t/, "→   ", tail)
        if (tail != "") tail = hl tail n
        printf "  %s│%s %s%3d%s  %s%s\n", c, n, d, NR, n, body, tail
      }'
  fi
  printf '  %s└──%s\n' "$color" "$N"
}

level_header() { # n
  local best; best=$(get_best "$1")
  printf '%s%s LEVEL %d/%d %s %s%s%s\n' "$MAG" "$B" "$1" "$NUM_LEVELS" "$N" "$B" "$TITLE" "$N"
  printf '%s par %d' "$D" "$PAR"
  [[ -n "$best" ]] && printf ' · best %d' "$best"
  printf '%s  %s\n\n' "$N" "$(star_string "$(level_stars "$1")")"
  load_level "$1"   # level_stars may have reloaded; be safe
}

# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
#  THE ED SESSION
# ═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# Sets globals: SESSION_COUNT, SESSION_TIME, SESSION_ABORTED, SESSION_OUTPUT
run_session() { # workdir
  local work=$1
  SESSION_COUNT=0 SESSION_ABORTED=0 SESSION_OUTPUT=''
  local t0=$SECONDS line rc

  printf '\n%s  ── entering ed. w to write, q to quit. ::hint ::target ::abort ──%s\n' "$D" "$N"

  # ed runs as a coprocess: we read your lines, count them, and forward them.
  # -r = restricted (no shell escapes, no files outside the level directory)
  # -v = verbose errors, because a bare '?' is a lot to ask of a newcomer.
  coproc EDPROC { cd "$work" && exec "$ED_BIN" -v -r -p "$ED_PROMPT" buffer.txt >/dev/tty 2>&1; }
  local pid=$EDPROC_PID fdw=${EDPROC[1]} fdr=${EDPROC[0]}

  trap 'printf "\n"' INT   # ed handles ^C itself (prints ?); we just survive it

  while kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; do
    IFS= read -r -t 0.2 line
    rc=$?
    if (( rc > 128 )); then
      continue                      # timeout or ^C: loop to re-check ed is alive
    elif (( rc != 0 )); then
      break                         # EOF (^D)
    fi

    case $line in
      ::t|::target)
        show_text "TARGET" "$GRN" "$TARGET"; printf '%s' "$ED_PROMPT"; continue ;;
      ::h|::hint)
        printf '%s%s hint:%s %s\n%s' "$YEL" "$B" "$N" "$HINT" "$ED_PROMPT"; continue ;;
      ::c|::count)
        printf '%s%d commands so far (par %d)%s\n%s' "$D" "$SESSION_COUNT" "$PAR" "$N" "$ED_PROMPT"; continue ;;
      ::a|::abort)
        SESSION_ABORTED=1; printf 'Q\n' >&"$fdw" 2>/dev/null; break ;;
      ::*)
        printf '%sunknown meta command; try ::hint ::target ::count ::abort%s\n%s' "$RED" "$N" "$ED_PROMPT"; continue ;;
    esac

    printf '%s\n' "$line" >&"$fdw" 2>/dev/null || break
    (( SESSION_COUNT++ ))
  done

  exec {fdw}>&- {fdr}<&- 2>/dev/null
  # give ed a moment to wind down, then insist
  local i
  for ((i = 0; i < 20; i++)); do kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || break; sleep 0.05; done
  kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null
  wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null
  trap - INT

  SESSION_TIME=$(( SECONDS - t0 ))
  SESSION_OUTPUT=$(cat "$work/buffer.txt" 2>/dev/null; printf x)
  SESSION_OUTPUT=${SESSION_OUTPUT%x}
  echo
}

setup_workdir() { # -> prints workdir path
  local work; work=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/edquest.XXXXXX") || exit 1
  if [[ -z "$START" ]]; then : > "$work/buffer.txt"; else printf '%s\n' "$START" > "$work/buffer.txt"; fi
  [[ -n "$EXTRA_NAME" ]] && printf '%s\n' "$EXTRA_CONTENT" > "$work/$EXTRA_NAME"
  printf '%s' "$work"
}

expected_bytes() { [[ -z "$TARGET" ]] && return; printf '%s\n' "$TARGET"; }

celebrate() { # count par time
  local c=$1 p=$2 t=$3 s; s=$(stars_for "$c" "$p")
  local msgs=( "The file is correct. Ken would be proud." "Flawless. The teletype hums approvingly."
               "Correct! ed printed nothing, which is its way of saying 'great job'."
               "Solved. Somewhere, a vi user feels a disturbance." )
  printf '\n  %s%s✔ SOLVED%s  %s\n' "$GRN" "$B" "$N" "${msgs[RANDOM % ${#msgs[@]}]}"
  printf '  commands: %s%d%s  (par %d)   time: %ds   %s\n' "$B" "$c" "$N" "$p" "$t" "$(star_string "$s")"
  if (( c < p )); then
    printf '  %s%s🏆 UNDER PAR! You out-ed the reference solution.%s\n' "$YEL" "$B" "$N"
  fi
}

play_level() { # n
  local n=$1 attempts=0 key work
  while true; do
    load_level "$n"
    cls
    level_header "$n"
    printf '%s\n\n' "$BRIEF" | sed 's/^/  /'
    show_text "START   (buffer.txt)" "$BLU" "$START"

I've built **ED QUEST**: a puzzle game with 20 levels where you edit text files in a real `ed` session. All 20 levels pass the built-in self-test. I also played a few levels through a real terminal: a correct answer, a wrong one, the in-game hint, and quitting without saving. Each gave the right result, and progress saved correctly.

```bash
cd edquest
./edquest.sh              # play
./edquest.sh --selftest   # check every level's built-in solution
./edquest.sh --reset      # wipe saved progress
```

**How it plays:**
- Each level shows a starting file and a target file.
- Press Enter and you're in `ed` on the starting file. Make it match the target, then save with `w` and quit with `q`.
- If your file is right, you get a score. If it isn't, you see a diff of how it differs from the target. If you quit without saving, it asks whether you forgot `w`.
- **Scoring:** the game counts every line you send to `ed`. Matching the built-in solution's length (par) earns ★★★, and beating it earns an "UNDER PAR" trophy. Best scores are saved in `~/.local/share/edquest/progress`.
- **Commands at the `ed>` prompt** (not counted): `::hint`, `::target`, `::count`, `::abort`.
- **No cheating:** `ed` runs in restricted mode (`-r`), so no shell escapes, and it can't read the answer file, which is kept in a separate folder.
- Error messages are verbose by default, because a bare `?` is a harsh welcome. Trailing spaces and tabs are highlighted so you can see them.

**Levels:** they start with `a`, `.`, `w` and `q`, then work through delete, append, insert, change, substitute, `g` and `v`, moving and copying lines, joining lines, regex groups, and indenting. Later puzzles cover stripping trailing whitespace, the classic `g/^/m0` line reversal, `r` (read a file in), moving a whole section, and splitting lines with `s`. The last level is a "final boss" that combines several of these.

There's also a pocket reference card for `ed`, and your rank goes from "?" up to "THE STANDARD TEXT EDITOR" as you collect stars. Choosing quit from the menu prints `?`.

I put it in its own `edquest/` folder so it stays separate from your course project files.
